trust_decision.summary: A bearer token is trusted as an OpenFGA principal only when its RS256 signature, expiry, `iss` (main issuer or alias), optional `sub` and - iff an audience is configured - its `aud` claim validate; at the pinned commit a blank audience silently drops the `aud` option, so any validly-signed token from the trusted issuer is accepted for any audience.

landing_point.why: It is the only place the `aud` claim is checked: jwt.WithAudience is appended only when strings.TrimSpace(oidc.Audience) is non-empty, so an unset --authn-oidc-audience turns the audience check off without any error.

fix_sites.entry_point: oidc.NewRemoteOidcAuthenticator (public constructor; production caller cmd/run/run.go:554 when authn.method=oidc)
RemoteOidcAuthenticator.Authenticate, reached by every gRPC/HTTP bearer-token request via the auth interceptors (cmd/run/run.go:634,638)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The codebase validates authn prerequisites only inside authenticator constructors (NewPresharedKeyAuthenticator rejects zero keys at internal/authn/presharedkey/presharedkey.go:25-28, exercised at cmd/run/run_test.go:206-216), and the new constructor error already aborts startup, so the config.VerifyBinarySettings gate looks redundant and can be skipped.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Whitespace-only issuer/audience are valid StringOrURI values (RFC 7519 4.1.1/4.1.3) and must still be accepted (the fix's tests assert "   " is a valid config), and non-oidc configs keep empty issuer/audience and must still verify - a TrimSpace/blank-based or method-unscoped guard breaks both.

O6_input_shapes: empty string audience (the reported case: --authn-oidc-audience unset)
both issuer and audience empty (issuer error is reported first)
whitespace-only value "   " (valid StringOrURI, must be accepted and then enforced literally)
constructor argument vs value arriving through the config file / env / flag merge

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same file already couples flags this way for access-control (:147) and both TLS pairs (:157, :171), and a maintainer would plausibly think the flags are the only way the value arrives, leaving config-file/env callers open.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: per-method prerequisite check inside authenticatorConfig before the oidc constructor call
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: That method switch is the only production caller of NewRemoteOidcAuthenticator and already returns constructor errors for preshared keys, so it is a natural place for a config precondition.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: fail-closed guard in Authenticate: if oidc.Audience == "" return errInvalidClaims
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The struct's fields are exported and the package's own tests build &RemoteOidcAuthenticator{} directly (internal/authn/oidc/oidc_test.go:30), so a maintainer adding defence-in-depth at the sink is realistic.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the same oidc issuer/audience requirement in VerifyServerSettings instead of VerifyBinarySettings
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Config.Verify() calls both verifiers (config.go:489-494), so either function is a plausible home for the check; a solver that patches one still passes Verify().

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a runtime enforcement of the schema's "required": ["issuer", "audience"] for the oidc definition
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The schema is published as the config contract and Config carries the comment to keep it in sync (pkg/server/config/config.go:366-367), so a maintainer could reasonably believe the requirement was already enforced.
